**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the age policy when computing upgrade nudges**

When `experimental.agenticAutoUpgrade` is `latest`, `future`, or `security`, the dev/build nudge still calls `getUpgradeAssessment` without the new age-policy argument, so this default bypasses the gate and can stop a command to recommend a release that the same project's explicit upgrade will reject or replace with an older eligible target. This occurs whenever a new reminder-worthy release is younger than the configured minimum age; resolve and pass the effective package policy from the nudge path as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept plain-string registry config output**

With supported pnpm 10.33, `pnpm config get --help` describes `get` as printing the config value and reserves JSON formatting for configuration lists; correspondingly, the exact `pnpm config get registry --json` invocation used here returns the unquoted string `https://registry.npmjs.org/`. `JSON.parse` therefore throws whenever a positive pnpm age gate causes `getAgeGateRegistry` to read either the default or scoped registry, preventing age-gated upgrades before any metadata request is made. Preserve raw string values when the output is not JSON (the duplicated codemod config reader has the same issue).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve standalone codemod targets through the age gate**

For a documented standalone invocation such as an old-enough `@next/codemod` running `upgrade latest`, `minor`, or `patch`, the target Next.js version is still selected earlier via unrestricted `npm view`; this newly added exact-version validation then throws whenever that newest release is too young, even if an older matching release is eligible. The fresh evidence in the final code is that the added loop only rejects the npm-selected target, so resolve the target with `ageEligibleVersions` before fetching its metadata instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Authenticate packument requests to configured registries**

When the effective registry is an authenticated corporate proxy or private mirror, this raw `fetch` sends none of the credentials that npm, pnpm, Yarn, or Bun would derive from their configuration. The package manager can therefore access the registry while age resolution receives a 401 and blocks every upgrade with a positive age gate; fetch metadata through an authenticated package-manager client/command or safely apply the effective registry credentials.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Non\-age\-gated stable apps fail `next upgrade --ai=latest/future` with \"Could not determine the latest stable Next\.js version\" because the canary CLI tooling version is forwarded as the upgrade target\.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle SIGHUP while the parent owns raw input**

When a process manager sends `SIGHUP` directly to the outer CLI while the menu is open on a persistent PTY, only `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` are handled here. Node's default `SIGHUP` termination bypasses the JavaScript `exit` callbacks, so neither `promptUpgrade()` nor the parent exit hook restores the terminal or performs orderly worker shutdown. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier resolved supervisor-signal thread is that the final rewrite removes `onHangup` entirely; register `SIGHUP` so it aborts the prompt, stops the child, and exits with signal status 129.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve failed dismissals for the CLI session**

When writing the “Skip until next version” preference fails—for example because the global config directory is read-only—`nudgeUpgradeForHuman()` warns that it is skipping for this session but still returns `dismiss`. This branch only reports plain `skip` to the parent, so no `skippedUpgradePolicy` is retained and any subsequent worker restart offers the same prompt again. Relay `dismiss` as a session skip as well, while still letting the worker attempt persistence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record Skip before sending it to the worker**

When an unrelated config or memory-threshold restart races with the user pressing Enter on Skip, this send targets the exiting worker and the callback intentionally tolerates the closed IPC channel. The parent only records `skippedUpgradePolicy` after that worker echoes `upgradePromptAction: 'skip'`, so the choice is lost and the replacement worker opens the prompt again. The fresh issue beyond the earlier IPC-closure fix is that the crash is suppressed but the session-level Skip semantics are not preserved; record the policy in the parent before attempting this send.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Send distDir with pre-ready upgrade prompts**

When the assessment finishes before the initial server startup and the user immediately selects Upgrade, this IPC payload contains no `distDir`; the parent does not learn it until `nextServerReady` (`next-dev.ts:567-569`). Consequently `handleSessionStop()` uses `.next` for telemetry and skips trace upload plus `writeDevState()` entirely for projects with a custom dist directory. The previous `nextUpgradeContext` message populated this value before opening the menu, so include it in the prompt IPC or otherwise initialize it before allowing Upgrade.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep direct-only Node flags out of NODE_OPTIONS**

When an inspected build is launched with another direct Node flag, such as `node --inspect --prof next build`, `getParsedNodeOptions()` collects both flags but `formatNodeOptions()` places `--prof` into `debugOptions.nodeOptions`, which this line assigns to `NODE_OPTIONS`. The child then aborts before running the build: Node v20.20.2's `--help` lists `--prof` as the V8 profiling option, while `NODE_OPTIONS=--prof node -e ''` exits 9 with `--prof is not allowed in NODE_OPTIONS`. Preserve direct-only entries from the original `process.execArgv` when rewriting the inspector address.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for the upgrade IPC message before exiting**

When compilation has already completed while the menu remains open, selecting Upgrade now queues this asynchronous `process.send()`, resolves `pendingUpgradeNudge`, and lets the child immediately reach `process.exit(0)` in `next.ts`. Because the send has no callback or acknowledgment and `process.exit()` does not drain pending IPC, the update message can be dropped; the parent then sees a normal child exit and silently skips the upgrade the user selected. Wait for IPC delivery or a parent acknowledgment before allowing the build child to complete.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

```suggestion // A prompt-driven interrupt (Ctrl+C in the raw-mode menu) is delivered // as an IPC message, so the child can finish and exit 0 before/despite // our `SIGINT`. Treat a 0 exit as an interrupt (130) while still // surfacing a genuine non-zero build failure code. process.exitCode = exit.signal ? 128 + constants.signals[exit.signal] : exit.code || 130 ``` An interrupted build \(Ctrl\+C in the upgrade menu\) is reported as a successful exit `0` instead of `130` because `exit.code ?? 130` keeps the child\'s `0` exit code\.

:robot: Fixed in 8875c5a4f75 with the regression test in 90e52639f50. The worker now includes its assessed policy when it opens the menu. Selecting Upgrade now makes the parent start shutdown and runUpgrade directly, without waiting for the worker to process another IPC message; Skip and dismissal still return to the worker. The real CLI test pauses the worker with SIGSTOP after the menu opens and verifies that upgrade preparation starts before the worker resumes. The focused webpack test passed, as did the package build and root TypeScript check.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Forward SIGUSR2 to memory-debug builds**

For an interactive `next build --experimental-debug-memory-usage`, this supervisor becomes the command PID but forwards only SIGINT, SIGTERM, and SIGHUP. The documented on-demand snapshot mechanism is installed only in the child (`lib/memory/startup.ts:20-29`), so sending SIGUSR2 to the launched command process—as directed by `docs/01-app/02-guides/memory-usage.mdx:50-54`—hits the supervisor's default signal behavior instead of writing a heap snapshot and can leave the actual build child running. Forward SIGUSR2 to the child when memory debugging is enabled.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Force an interrupt status after prompt Ctrl+C**

When compilation has already finished and is waiting only for the menu, pressing Ctrl+C makes the child send `upgradePromptAction: 'interrupt'` and then immediately complete `nextBuild`, after which the CLI calls `process.exit(0)`. The parent can therefore set `interrupted` but still observe `exit.code === 0`, and this expression prefers that zero over the intended 130, reporting the interrupted build as successful. The fresh evidence versus the earlier resolved interrupt finding is this revision's new child/IPC flow and its explicit reuse of the child's clean exit code; record prompt interrupts separately and force status 130, or handshake before allowing the child to exit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Await the nudge before generate-env returns**

When a human TTY runs `next build --experimental-build-mode generate-env` with an upgrade policy enabled, this promise is started but never awaited: both generate-env branches return at `build/index.ts:1256` or `1269`, before the shared await at line 4740. The child consequently reaches the CLI's explicit `process.exit(0)` while the assessment or menu is still pending, so the configured prompt can disappear or never be shown and the parent reports a successful build. Await the pending nudge on these early-success paths as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle Upgrade without waiting on a stalled worker**

If the dev worker becomes synchronously blocked after opening the menu—for example, in a bundler task or request handler—the parent accepts Upgrade and prints its confirmation but only queues this choice to that worker. Shutdown and `runUpgrade()` begin only after the worker processes the message and echoes `upgradePromptAction: 'update'`, so the selected upgrade never starts while the worker remains blocked, even though the parent intentionally handles Ctrl+C locally for this scenario. Include the policy in the initial prompt message and handle Upgrade in the responsive parent as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

:robot: Fixed in cb03e00add5 (now on PR #99191 as ef772da336b). Both prompt-choice sends share a callback that tolerates ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED if the worker disconnects during restart and logs other send errors with their cause. The build stack was rebased onto this change. TypeScript, Prettier, ESLint, and diff checks passed.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align the ordinary canary target with the codemod**

When `next upgrade canary` runs with a stricter age policy for scoped `@next/codemod` than for unscoped `next`, these independent lookups can select an older codemod canary and a newer Next.js canary. Both packages satisfy their individual policies, so the command runs, but the older executable can lack migrations introduced for the selected target and leave the application incompletely upgraded. Select the newest canary version that is eligible and published for both packages.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve Bun's global config through the OS home directory**

On Windows when `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` are unset—as is common in PowerShell—but `USERPROFILE` is set, this produces no global Bun config path even though Bun resolves `~/.bunfig.toml` from the user's OS home directory. A globally configured minimum release age is therefore read as zero, so the upgrade chooses a release that the subsequent `bunx` invocation can reject. Use `os.homedir()` (while preserving XDG precedence) rather than relying solely on `HOME`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Age-gate dependencies selected by the codemod**

When `next` and `@next/codemod` are old enough but a compatible React, React DOM, types, or optional Next.js package release is newer than the configured gate, checking only these two package ages is insufficient. `packages/next-codemod/bin/upgrade.ts` independently selects the highest matching React and types versions through `npm view`, writes those exact versions, and then invokes the selected package manager, which rejects the young release. Resolve every dynamically selected install version against the effective age policy, or make the codemod perform age-aware resolution.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the age gate to stable AI upgrade targets**

When a stable app with a positive minimum release age runs `next upgrade --ai=latest` or `--ai=future`, this condition ignores the resolved age-eligible version because `channel` is `null`; the function then fetches the unrestricted `latest` stable tag. If that release is newer than the configured gate, the generated upgrade still targets an exact version that the selected package manager refuses to install. Resolve an age-eligible stable target as well as an eligible canary runner.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

:robot: We reviewed this test gate and chose to keep the existing mode check. This shared E2E file also contains build coverage; the dev-only cases remain skipped outside dev mode. No code change is planned for this suggestion.

:robot: Fixed in ce29e6d8f3b. The parent CLI owns the prompt input and handles Ctrl+C itself, so a blocked dev worker cannot prevent the interrupt from reaching the parent. The focused blocked-worker PTY check passed.
:robot: Fixed in ce29e6d8f3b. The surviving parent now restores terminal mode during forced shutdown, including when the worker cannot run its own prompt cleanup.

:robot: Fixed in ce29e6d8f3b. A signal exit from the dev worker now calls handleSessionStop with the corresponding signal exit status, so the outer CLI exits instead of remaining alive without a worker.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle IPC closure when returning prompt choices**

When the dev worker exits or restarts between the `worker.connected` check and this send—for example, a `next.config` edit races with the user pressing Enter—`ChildProcess.send()` can emit an asynchronous `ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED` error. Because this child has no `error` listener and the send has no callback, that error can terminate the outer CLI instead of allowing the configured worker restart; send the reply with an error-handling callback or otherwise tolerate the channel closing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make default package-manager detection recognize Bun**

When an AI upgrade in a Bun project prepares an adoption skill or generates its cross-major codemod command, those call sites still invoke `getNpxCommand(baseDir)` without the newly detected manager. This default calls `getPkgManager`, which recognizes neither Bun's `bun/…` user agent nor `bun.lock` and whose return type cannot be `bun`, so the new `bunx` branch is unreachable and the prompt uses npm, pnpm, or Yarn instead, bypassing the Bun release-age policy. Pass the detected manager through these AI paths or add Bun to the shared detector.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep a newer invoking canary instead of relaunching an older one**

When the project already has a canary newer than the age cutoff—for example, the policy was enabled or increased after that version was installed—the age resolver returns an older canary and this inequality relaunches the upgrade with that older CLI. That CLI may predate `upgrade --ai` or lack guides and assessment logic needed by the installed version, even though the already-running CLI requires no installation and therefore does not violate the package-manager gate. Only delegate when the selected eligible canary is newer than the invoking CLI.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a Windows-safe launcher for package-manager shims**

On Windows, npm, pnpm, and Yarn are normally exposed as `.cmd` shims, which Node cannot execute directly through `execFileSync` without a shell. Every upgrade now reaches this helper merely to probe the manager version, even when the installed manager is too old to implement an age gate, so these upgrades fail before their previous cross-platform launch path is reached. Use the bundled `cross-spawn` handling or the same `execSync` fallback already used by `next-info.ts`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve minor and patch revisions through the age gate**

When a pnpm, Yarn, or Bun project with a positive age gate runs `next upgrade --revision minor` or `--revision patch`, neither revision enters this allowlist. `packages/next-codemod/bin/upgrade.ts` supports those keywords but resolves their ranges with `npm view`, which does not know the selected manager's policy, and then asks that manager to install the newest exact version; if it is too new, the upgrade still fails. Convert these keywords to the corresponding semver range and select an age-eligible version before launching the codemod.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor version-qualified age-gate exclusions**

When an exclusion names a particular allowed version, such as pnpm's supported `next@17.0.0-canary.35` form, matching only the bare package name always returns false. The repository itself uses this version-qualified exclusion syntax in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and Yarn also accepts package descriptors, so the resolver can skip the explicitly exempt release and choose an older version or report that none is eligible. Exclusion matching needs the candidate version as well as the package name.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the codemod when resolving the AI canary**

When an AI upgrade crosses a major and `@next/codemod` has a stricter age policy than `next`—for example, `next` is excluded or Yarn applies a scoped policy—this resolves eligibility for `next` alone. The generated cross-major command later pins `@next/codemod` to that same CLI version, so the package manager can reject it as too new; resolve a version shared by both packages here, as the non-AI canary path already does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the configured registry for age resolution**

When a pnpm, Yarn, npm, or Bun project installs through a corporate registry or an npm mirror, this hard-coded URL bypasses that configuration. An age-gated upgrade can therefore fail while fetching metadata from the public registry, or select a version that the configured mirror has not synchronized, even though the package-manager command itself would use the configured registry. Resolve packuments through the manager's effective registry instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

On Yarn 4\.10\/4\.11\, an unset `npmMinimalAgeGate` makes `readJsonConfig` return `null`\, which is passed unguarded to `parseNonNegativeNumber` and throws `Invalid npmMinimalAgeGate value` instead of returning `0` \(no gate\)\.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate the dev-only suite instead of hard-skipping it**

This runtime `it.skip` branch bypasses the repository's gate-condition validation and reporting for every non-dev shard. Mark the `describe` with a static `// @force-gate dev` directive and remove the conditional placeholder so the test matrix records the suite's actual execution constraint through the standard gate infrastructure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep Ctrl+C handling outside the dev worker**

When the menu is open and the dev worker's event loop becomes synchronously blocked—for example by an infinite loop in a route, config hook, or bundler task—the prompt's raw terminal mode turns Ctrl+C into an input byte instead of a `SIGINT`. Because the keypress handler now runs in that same blocked worker, it cannot send the interrupt IPC message, while the otherwise-responsive outer CLI never receives a signal and therefore cannot terminate the hung worker. Keep the terminal interrupt proxy in the parent or otherwise let the parent receive Ctrl+C independently of the worker event loop.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore terminal mode before force-killing the prompt worker**

When an external `SIGTERM` reaches the outer CLI while this worker-owned menu is open and application shutdown exceeds the default 100 ms grace period, `next-dev.ts` force-kills the worker with `SIGKILL`. The prompt restores raw input only from its worker's `exit` listener, which `SIGKILL` cannot run, so a directly spawned CLI under a persistent PTY or task runner leaves that terminal in raw mode after Next exits. Abort and restore the menu before beginning worker shutdown, or have the surviving parent restore the shared terminal before force-killing the worker.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Shut down when the dev worker dies by signal**

When the supervised worker is killed directly by a signal, such as an OOM `SIGKILL` or task tooling targeting the worker PID while the menu is open, this return leaves the outer `next dev` CLI alive with no server and no worker capable of sending a prompt action. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier resolved thread is that the final worker-owned rewrite removed the `upgradeInProgress` shutdown fallback and reinstated this unconditional return; signal exits should terminate the outer session with the corresponding status.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The new commits already added the exact fix proposed by this suggestion\. In `packages/next/src/cli/next-build.ts`\, `onHangup` \(which calls `saveCpuProfile()` then `process.exit(129)`\) is now registered unconditionally at lines 46\-53\:

```ts
const onHangup = () => {
  saveCpuProfile()
  process.exit(129)
}
process.on('SIGTERM', onTerminate)
process.on('SIGINT', onInterrupt)
process.on('SIGHUP', onHangup)
```

Both paths are covered\: the direct path \(nextBuild handles SIGHUP itself\) and the fork path \(supervisor parent forwards SIGHUP via `child.kill('SIGHUP')` to the child running nextBuild\, which now saves the CPU profile\)\. The CPU profile is no longer lost on SIGHUP\.

New commits added `delete env.CI` and `delete env.GITHUB_ACTIONS` to `startDev()`\. On GitHub Actions\, those are the only CI markers the compiled `ci-info` detector reacts to\: `isCI = CI || CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION || BUILD_NUMBER || RUN_ID || name`\, where `name` for GitHub Actions is set only via `GITHUB_ACTIONS`\. GitHub Actions does not set bare `CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION`\, `BUILD_NUMBER`\, or `RUN_ID` \(it uses `GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`\/`GITHUB_RUN_ID`\)\, nor `NOW_BUILDER`\/`STACK` used by `server/ci-info.ts`\. With `CI` and `GITHUB_ACTIONS` removed\, the child `next dev` computes `isCI === false`\, so neither `canPromptForUpgrade()` \(`!isCI`\) nor the `if (requested && isCI) return` guard short\-circuits\, and the \"Upgrade now\" menu is shown\. The bug is resolved for the CI environment this test runs in\.

The new commits \(2b635e3\, 8f9f0a8\) reintroduced a once\-per\-session guard for the skip case via a different mechanism\. When the human chooses plain \"Skip\"\, `router-server.ts` sends `{ upgradePromptAction: 'skip', policy }` to the parent CLI\, which stores it in `skippedUpgradePolicy` \(next\-dev\.ts\:495\) and forwards it to every subsequently\-forked worker via `NEXT_PRIVATE_UPGRADE_SKIPPED_POLICY` \(next\-dev\.ts\:427\)\. On restart\, `router-server.ts` passes a `null` signal to `nudgeUpgrade` when `process.env.NEXT_PRIVATE_UPGRADE_SKIPPED_POLICY === policy`\, and `nudgeUpgrade`\'s human path returns early on a null signal \(nudge\.ts\:469\)\, so the full\-screen menu is not re\-shown\. This directly closes the concrete trigger the suggestion described \(plain \"Skip\" reappearing on every dev\-server restart\)\. The `'dismiss'` case is persisted via `getUpgradeDismissal`\, and `'update'`\/`'interrupt'` exit the session\, so all human outcomes are now covered\. The suggestion\'s patch also no longer applies\.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep worktree upgrades in the corresponding app directory**

When an existing agent, copied prompt, or non-TTY handoff resolves this factory with `useWorktree === null`, an unspecified choice still defaults to a separate worktree, but this branch drops the previous instruction to run from the app's corresponding directory there. For a monorepo app such as `/repo/apps/web`, the task summary continues to name the original checkout path, so the agent can run the upgrade at the new worktree root or modify the original app, defeating the requested isolation. Preserve the corresponding-app-directory instruction whenever the prompt may select a worktree.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Force the non-TTY branch in this test**

When this suite is run in-band from an interactive terminal, `process.stdin.isTTY` and `process.stdout.isTTY` remain true, so this test enters agent discovery instead of the intended non-TTY branch. With the reset `fs/promises` and `cross-spawn` mocks, discovery finds no harness and then reaches the undefined mocked `spawn.sync`, causing the test to fail.
